This mandatory inbound firewall is configured in a default deny-all mode to prevent unauthorized access and Amazon EC2 customers must explicitly open the ports needed to allow inbound traffic.
The customer is responsible for choosing which of their Virtual Private Clouds (VPCs) they want a file system to be accessed from by creating resources called mount targets.

Customers are responsible for securing these compute resources, for example if a customer uses Amazon EC2 for workers then they can restrict access to their instances in Amazon EC2 to specific AWS IAM users.

As an Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) System, the AWS System is designed based on a shared responsibility model where both AWS and the customers are responsible for aspects of security, availability and confidentiality.
Customers are responsible for the development, operation, maintenance, and use of their content.
Customers are responsible for determining what content to store within AWS, which may include personal information.
If required, customers are responsible for providing notice to the individuals whose data the customer collects and uses within AWS.
